evidence.actual: Every accepted control request creates a UUID command_id and commits REQUESTED before MQTT publication.
commands is authoritative current state; command_lifecycle_events is append-only durable history.
All accepted backend lifecycle mutations use row-locked transition authority; terminal states are immutable and duplicate same-state events are idempotent.
Retries reuse the same command_id; idempotency_key is uniquely scoped and conflicting reuse returns conflict.
Controller lifecycle events require matching device_id and known command_id before durable transition.
CONFIRMED remains gated by correlated authoritative runtime/controller observation; ACK does not imply physical confirmation.

evidence.notes: SENT and ACKNOWLEDGED deadlines produce TIMEOUT; ambiguous outbound attempts produce UNKNOWN; retry budget exhaustion produces FAILED.

evidence.actual: Startup/periodic reconciliation reads PostgreSQL active commands and resumes only eligible safe retries using the persisted command_id; terminal records are not reopened.
PASS; one concurrent transition is Applied and the other is Duplicate; retry_due uses UPDATE ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED atomic claim.
Command list/detail/history read from durable PostgreSQL state and remain behind existing P1.1 capability/ownership boundary.
Lifecycle AppEvent and compatibility system_events are emitted only after durable transition/create commit.

Current actuator control API is single-device; there is no bulk actuator-command route requiring command fan-out. Existing bulk recipe route authorizes all devices before mutation and returns per-device success/failure, so it does not claim whole-operation success from partial transport outcomes.
Durable request_payload is allowlisted to retry-safe command fields; privileged/API/WiFi/webhook secrets are excluded from lifecycle persistence.

15 durable lifecycle tests pass serially, covering creation, idempotency/conflict, transition/terminal immutability, duplicate transition concurrency, publish retry, timeout, UNKNOWN, retry safety, and secret-safe payload.

Backend cargo check/clippy/fmt verified; prior backend regression baseline was 364/364 before the final retry-safety change; shared/controller-core prior verification remains green. ESP32 application target check is blocked only by environment: esp-idf-sys reports Unsupported target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.
P1.2 implementation, verification, environmental firmware limitation, and phase boundary are recorded.

verification.database_schema: retry_safe column verified in live PostgreSQL

known_limitations: ESP32-C3 application target build cannot run in this host environment because ESP-IDF is being invoked for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.

A direct two-AppState integration test for retry_due claim contention is not present; the implementation uses an atomic PostgreSQL UPDATE with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and transition concurrency is directly tested.
No bulk actuator-control endpoint exists in the current API surface; AC-12 is therefore satisfied by explicit scope boundary plus existing all-device bulk recipe authorization semantics.
